My grandma knew it was coming for a few years. She was in her mid-90's so it wasn't really a surprise. She used to hit me with the "I won't be around forever" line. She lived a good life, was in the Navy in WW2, and kept her independence right up until she drowned, so we were all cool with it, even her.

It hit me harder later. When I wanted to call and he wasn't there. When I wanted to show him something. I kept it together for my mother, since it was her father and her only other living family. But it hit me harder later, when she was more or less stable again.

There's no right or wrong way to deal with death. And how you cope now might be different from how you cope for this loss or another in the future.

I'd say my biggest advice is self-care. Get an exercise habit going. Even 10 minutes of stretching is really good for your brain. It's easier to deal with all of this if you're a little healthy. Writing helps a lot, too. I recommend free writing, where you just write whatever comes into your head for however long, maybe 5 minutes. After that, you can focus more on one topic if it helps.

And one last thing. Consider recording some conversations with the ones still alive. Ask them about their past, growing up, the good times and the bad. That's your family history, and it's a record of people you love. This is the only chance you have to save their voices.
